body.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) and every regular conditional
law \(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}=P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\) of the complete causal-data
array given the realized query, attach the labels
\[
 \mu_{P,s}(z_0)=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}},
 \qquad m_P=(m_1,\ldots,m_S),
 \qquad \Sigma_P(z_0)=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}(Z_j),
\]
and write
\(\xi_P(z_0)=(\mathbb K_{P,z_0};\mu_P(z_0),m_P,\Sigma_P(z_0))\).
Then
\[
 \xi_P(z_0)\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)
\]
for \(P\)-almost every query value \(z_0\) under its marginal query law.
No membership assertion is made for a labelled point built from a version
of the conditional law at a query-null value.
body.justification: This lemma separates a fixed-query statistical experiment from the almost-everywhere disintegration that links it to a causal panel law.
body.gap: It does not select or regularize conditional versions at query-null values.
body.consumer: All fixed-query risk, coverage, and model-audit statements use this bridge when transferred back to the panel class.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) and a regular conditional law
\(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}=P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\).  Give it the labels displayed in
the statement.  We check the clauses of
\texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}.

The almost-sure consistency, boundedness, exact-design observation, and
interior conditions under \(P\) disintegrate to the corresponding
\(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}\)-almost-sure conditions outside a marginally null set
of query values.  The Holder condition is a property of each labelled
function \(m_s\) and is unchanged by conditioning.  Assumption
\texttt{ass:event-date-transport} gives, outside a marginally null set,
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_{0s}).
 \tag{1}
\]
The first equality in \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}[Q_{sti}\mid\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st}),
 \tag{2}
\]
and its second equality, together with the definition of
\(\mu_{P,s}(z_0)\), gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}
 [B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]=\mu_{P,s}(z_0).
 \tag{3}
\]
All three statements hold for almost every query.

Assumption \texttt{ass:design-density} explicitly supplies, for every
\(s,t\), a conditional density satisfying
\[
 c_X\le f_{st\mid z_0}(x)\le C_X
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1]^d
 \tag{4}
\]
for almost every query.  Assumption \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing} likewise
supplies
\[
 \beta_s(k\mid z_0)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1,
 \tag{5}
\]
for almost every query.  The conditional-independence assertions in
\texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}, \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, and
\texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} are factorization assertions for
these regular conditional laws and therefore hold for almost every query.

Finally, \texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness},
\texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}, and
\texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}, together with the definition of
\(\Sigma_P(z_0)\), give for almost every query
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}Z_j=z_0,
 \quad
 c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma_P(z_0)\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd},
 \quad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}\!\left[
 \|\Sigma_P(z_0)^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\right]\le B^4.
 \tag{6}
\]
The eigenvalue lower bound in (6) is strictly positive, so the inverse
square root exists.  Bounded wealth implies
\(|\mu_{P,s}(z_0)|\le B\), and the first identity in the statement and the
definition of \(\Sigma_P(z_0)\) verify the remaining label requirements.

There are finitely many cohorts, dates, and unit indices and only countably
many lags \(k\).  Intersecting all conull query sets used in (1)--(6)
therefore leaves a conull set.  At each query in this intersection, the
labelled point \(\xi_P(z_0)\) satisfies every member property of
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  This proves the assertion and says
nothing about an arbitrarily selected conditional version on the
complementary null set.
